subject: MAP: cross-region routing & failover — performance scan + next steps

Subject: MAP proposal: cross-region performance evaluation & close plan

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the trial credits and the quick onboarding call. Attached is a first-pass MAP / evaluation plan (MAP-eval-plan-v1.pdf) that outlines the tests FinWave needs to validate before we sign. High-level goals:

- Verify steady-state latency and TTFT across US / EU / APAC (p50/p95/p99)
- Measure throughput (tokens/sec) under target concurrency bands (50, 200, 800 concurrent sessions)
- Cold-start TTFT and warm KV-cache TTFT measurements
- Multi-region routing correctness and failover time under simulated AZ/region outage

Proposed timeline:
- Nov 30: Redwood runs baseline sweep (3 rounds) with our sample prompts
- Dec 1: Joint analysis, iterate on routing policy parameters
- Dec 3: Final MAP signoff and canary rollout plan

Please confirm: test accounts, any rate limits we should be aware of, and whether Redwood can run the simulated region failover (preferred) or if we should kick it off from our side.

Deliverables expected from Redwood after the run: CSV of raw traces, summary PDF with p50/p95/p99 and TTFT breakdown, and an artifact showing routing decision logs for failover windows.

Attachments: MAP-eval-plan-v1.pdf

Thanks,
Alex Jenkins

Alex — appreciate the clear plan. We're aligned on scope and can run the baseline and failover tests from our side. A few clarifications and asks before we kick off:

- Metrics to capture (we will include these in redwood-test-config.json): p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT (time to first token), tokens/sec throughput, connection-level cold vs warm TTFT, and KV-cache hit/miss markers.
- Failover test: we propose a staged failover where we shift routing from us-east -> eu-west -> ap-southeast and introduce a 45s regional blackout in each region to measure RTO and request continuity.
- Concurrency bands: we'll run 3 profiles (50, 200, 800) and do 3 full sweeps each for statistical confidence.
- Quantization/variant note: We'll test the customer's preferred model variant and a lower-latency quantized variant to show tradeoffs.

I attached our initial test config (redwood-test-config.json) — contains payload sizes, prompt templates, and the test harness TTLs. Two action items for us: Laura to validate infra pre-reqs and Marissa to coordinate access + HubSpot deal artifacts. Alex, confirm the sample prompt set is final or send changes.

We can start the runs on Nov 30 08:00 PST if that works for FinWave.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks

Team — quick checklist ahead of the 08:00 PST run today:

Subject: FinWave: regional scan results (initial)

Dylan / Laura — thanks for running the sweeps. Attached are the CSV of raw traces and a short PDF summary with initial observations (finwave-regional-scan-results.csv, finwave-map-results-summary.pdf). Highlights:

- US (us-west/us-east): steady p50 18–22ms, p95 75–90ms, p99 ~180ms. TTFT warm ~80ms, cold-start TTFT spikes up to 1.8s.
- EU (eu-west): median +10–15ms vs US at p50, p95 at ~120ms (likely routing overhead + inter-region hop).
- APAC (ap-southeast): variable. Warm TTFT 120–350ms depending on peak; we observed intermittent 2–3s TTFT spikes during the 800-concurrency sweep — possibly due to ephemeral instance spin or cold-KV misses.
- Failover window: we saw an average RTO of 52s when we simulated region withdrawal. Most user requests recovered after fallback to secondary region, but a small percentage (0.6%) experienced dropped sessions requiring retry logic.

Questions for Redwood: can you share the router decision logs for the failover windows and the precise timings for when routes were reprogrammed? Also would like to see the cold-start sub-trace for the 800-concurrency run.

Forwarding below is Laura's pre-run checklist for reference.

Regards,
Alex Jenkins
Senior Solutions Engineer, FinWave
Attachments: finwave-regional-scan-results.csv; finwave-map-results-summary.pdf
